## Discovery & Translational Science

- **Targeting TMPRSS6 in metabolic liver disease raises cardiovascular and lipid safety concerns** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.29.26366887)
  - Mendelian randomization analyzing genetic TMPRSS6 (matriptase-2) inhibition demonstrated lower liver iron content (β = -2.50, p < 0.001) but increased corrected T1 (cT1, β = 1.59, p < 0.001), indicating potential inflammatory or fibrotic exacerbation.
  - Genetically proxied inhibition was associated with elevated LDL cholesterol (β = 0.22, p < 0.001) and an increased risk of coronary artery disease (OR = 1.59, p < 0.001), highlighting target-mediated cardiovascular liabilities.

- **Biomarker research links parietal periodic gamma EEG activity to amyloid and tau pathology** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.30.26366850)
  - Resting-state EEG in cognitively normal older adults showed that higher amyloid-β PET burden correlates with elevated parietal periodic gamma power (β = +0.50, p = 0.025).
  - Periodic gamma moderated the relationship between amyloid-β and entorhinal tau accumulation (β = +0.90, p = 0.002 in amyloid-positive adults), pointing to early excitation-inhibition imbalance as a driver of tau progression.

- **Extracellular Ca²⁺ protects vascular endothelium from cytotoxic histone injury** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.07.13.664578)
  - Live-cell imaging revealed that extracellular Ca²⁺ acts via charge screening to prevent cytotoxic histone binding to anionic membrane phospholipids in human endothelial cells and mouse mesenteric arteries.
  - Protection occurred independently of ORAI-mediated store-operated Ca²⁺ entry, clarifying endothelial vulnerability mechanisms during trauma- and sepsis-induced hypocalcemia.

- **VEGFR-3-driven lymphangiogenesis identified as essential for laryngotracheal repair** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.19.745806)
  - Murine injury models demonstrated marked expansion of subepithelial LYVE-1⁺ lymphatic vessel density during airway mucosal healing.
  - Selective pharmacologic blockade of VEGFR-3 via SAR131675 impaired epithelial repair, heightened mucosal edema, and significantly increased mortality, identifying lymphangiogenesis as a necessary tissue-repair mechanism.

- **CLEC10A defines an MHC class II-high myeloid niche in neuroblastoma** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.30.26366893)
  - Multi-cohort single-cell and spatial profiling identified CLEC10A as a marker for MHC class II-high tumor-associated monocytes and macrophages residing in T-cell-rich microenvironments in MYCN non-amplified neuroblastoma.

- **Computational and natural product drug discovery platforms updated**
  - **THEOBROMA** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42969050/): Released an aggregated open database of 1.13 million natural products with stereochemistry-aware deduplication and auditing.
  - **RNAactDrug 2.0** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42969048/): Updated multi-omics computational framework mapping molecular features to drug sensitivity.
  - **Medicinal chemistry trends** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42968521/): Published analysis highlighting synthetic reaction stagnation and its restrictive impact on chemical space diversity in lead optimization.

## Early Trials — Phase I–II

- **[Biotech]** **Agenus reports positive Phase 2 UNICORN data for neoadjuvant botensilimab/balstilimab in colon cancer** [Nature Medicine](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04710-1)
  - The Phase 2 UNICORN trial met its primary endpoint, demonstrating high major pathological response rates with short-course neoadjuvant botensilimab (Fc-enhanced anti-CTLA-4) plus balstilimab (anti-PD-1).
  - Efficacy was observed across both mismatch repair-proficient (pMMR) and mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) colon cancer cohorts.

- **[Biotech]** **Kymera Therapeutics awaits Phase 2 readout for oral degrader candidate in eczema** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/pharmalot/2026/11/02/drugmaker-payments-to-russian-middlemen-possible-dupixent-rival/)
  - Mid-stage trial readouts are imminent for Kymera's targeted protein degrader, positioned as an oral alternative to injected IL-4/IL-13 biologics like Dupixent (dupilumab) in moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis.

- **[Biotech]** **Enlivex Therapeutics reports 12-month Phase 1/2a data for Allocetra** [X / Twitter](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2117241102730404141)
  - Topline 12-month follow-up data from the Phase 1/2a trial of cell therapy candidate Allocetra demonstrated durable treatment responses.

- **First-in-human Phase 1 study published for oral C5aR inhibitor izicopan (INF904)** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42968369/)
  - A randomized, placebo-controlled single and multiple ascending dose trial established the safety, pharmacokinetics, and target engagement of izicopan, an oral small-molecule complement C5a receptor inhibitor, in healthy volunteers.

- **Phase 2 METIS trial evaluates neoadjuvant regimens in HER2⁺ breast cancer** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42967914/)
  - Randomized trial assessed pathological complete response rates of concurrent versus sequential anthracycline-containing chemotherapy combined with anti-HER2 targeted therapy in the neoadjuvant setting.

## Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III

- **[Biotech]** **Incyte’s oral JAK1 inhibitor povorcitinib wins in twin Phase 3 vitiligo trials** [Nature Medicine](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04739-2)
  - Phase 3 STOP-V1 and STOP-V2 trials demonstrated that oral povorcitinib achieved statistically significant superiority over placebo in reaching F-VASI75 response thresholds in adult nonsegmental vitiligo.

- **[Big Pharma]** **AstraZeneca delays Phase 3 Avanzar trial readout of Dato-DXd to H1 2027** [X / Twitter](https://x.com/JacobPlieth/status/2117199460753432993)
  - AstraZeneca and Daiichi Sankyo postponed the primary readout for the Phase 3 Avanzar study evaluating TROP2-directed ADC datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd) plus Imfinzi in first-line NSCLC to H1 2027.

- **[Big Pharma]** **Higher-dose CagriSema delivers superior weight loss in Phase 3 meta-analysis** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.30.26366916)
  - Meta-analysis of 1,506 patients across three Phase 3 trials showed CagriSema (cagrilintide/semaglutide) 2.4/2.4 mg yielded a -2.07 percentage point greater body weight reduction compared to the 1.0/1.0 mg dose, with 64.9% vs. 55.1% achieving ≥10% body weight loss.
  - Glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) reduction did not differ significantly between doses (-0.16 percentage points), while gastrointestinal adverse events were more frequent in the high-dose group (64.8% vs. 53.2%).

- **Phase 3 meta-analysis ranks 2-year eGFR slope preservation in IgA nephropathy** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.29.26366792)
  - Network meta-analysis of 2,437 patients across six Phase 3 trials showed dual and single APRIL/BAFF inhibitors (telitacicept +5.1, atacicept +5.0, sibeprenlimab +4.7 mL/min/1.73m²/year vs. placebo) offered the highest preservation of annualized eGFR slope, yielding a pooled 98% attenuation of slope decline.
  - APRIL/BAFF targeting agents outperformed complement factor B inhibitor iptacopan (+3.0), targeted-release budesonide (+1.8), and endothelin receptor antagonist atrasentan (+1.4).

- **Phase 3 trial evaluates 3× daily 5% diquafosol in dry eye disease** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42968636/)
  - Randomized, double-masked Phase 3 trial established that thrice-daily 5% diquafosol ophthalmic solution met noninferiority criteria relative to the standard six-times-daily 3% diquafosol regimen.

- **PCI guidance trial compares CCTA against intravascular ultrasound** [NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2610771?af=R&rss=currentIssue)
  - Head-to-head trial evaluated coronary CT angiography (CCTA) guidance against intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) guidance during percutaneous coronary intervention.

## Regulatory & Approvals

- **[Big Pharma]** **FDA accepts BLA for first Keytruda biosimilar FYB206** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/keytruda-biosimilars-fda-pbm-market-share-drug/873424/)
  - The FDA accepted Formycon's BLA for FYB206, a biosimilar referencing Merck & Co.’s pembrolizumab (Keytruda), with potential approval targeted for Q3 2027.
  - Over a dozen biosimilars are in development ahead of Keytruda's initial 2028 patent expirations, though commercial launch dynamics remain constrained by existing PBM rebate structures.

- **[Biotech]** **FDA places partial clinical hold on Bright Minds Biosciences' BMB-101 trial** [X / Twitter](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2117243647317979573)
  - The FDA placed a partial clinical hold on the clinical trial program for BMB-101, an oral selective 5-HT₂C receptor agonist in development for absence seizures and developmental epileptic encephalopathies.

- **FDA approves generic injectable lenacapavir for HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/pharmalot/2026/11/02/lenacapavir-generic-version-approved-fda-hiv-prevention-dr-reddys/)
  - The FDA approved a generic version of injectable lenacapavir for HIV PrEP under global access initiatives, opening low-cost manufacturing routes for lower-income countries.

## Business & Strategy

- **[Big Pharma]** **AstraZeneca launches $1.5B restructuring effort to fund R&D engine** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/astrazeneca-alnylam-regeneron-3q26-earnings-analysis/873410/)
  - AstraZeneca announced "Reshaping for Sustainable Growth," a restructuring plan designed to generate $1.5 billion in annual cost savings for reinvestment into core drug discovery.
  - Management reiterated its $80 billion revenue target by 2030, citing 20 upcoming late-stage trial readouts over the next 12 months with >$20 billion in total peak revenue potential.

- **[Big Pharma]** **Teva halts Phase 2 MSA trial of emrusolmin after futility analysis** [X / Twitter](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2117240732042104892)
  - Teva Pharmaceutical is discontinuing the Phase 2 TOPAS-MSA study of emrusolmin (TEV-48286) in multiple system atrophy following a pre-planned interim futility assessment.

- **[Biotech]** **Karyopharm Therapeutics files Chapter 11 bankruptcy, agrees to Ayrmid merger** [X / Twitter](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2117243221566701770)
  - Karyopharm Therapeutics initiated Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings alongside a definitive agreement to merge with Ayrmid Ltd.

- **[Biotech]** **Krystal Biotech authorizes $400M share buyback** [X / Twitter](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2117240575774822402)
  - Krystal Biotech’s board of directors authorized a share repurchase program of up to $400 million.

## Public Health & Policy

- **Long-term EHR study reveals persistent post-COVID-19 neurological risks** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.30.26366919)
  - Analysis of 18.3 million UK primary care records showed elevated incidence of cognitive impairment and dementia lasting up to 4 years post-infection (aHR 4.02 pre-vaccination; aHR 2.24 post-vaccination).
  - Excess risk was heavily elevated among individuals hospitalized during acute infection and partially attenuated by prior vaccination.

- **Off-label commercial marketing of mitochondrial replacement therapy draws scrutiny** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/02/three-parent-ivf-fertility-tourism-investigation-mrt-therapy/)
  - An investigation into global fertility clinics highlights the commercial promotion of mitochondrial replacement therapy (MRT, three-parent IVF) for age-related infertility, despite a lack of clinical efficacy evidence and original regulatory approvals restricted to preventing inherited mitochondrial diseases.

- **High acceptability reported for event-driven PrEP among South African cisgender men** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.30.26366952)
  - A survey of 150 cisgender men in Cape Town found 86.7% acceptability for event-driven HIV PrEP (ED-PrEP), supporting non-daily administration options to improve regimen adherence.

- **Framework reassesses pediatric enrollment in high-risk first-in-human trials** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42967310/)
  - An ethical review outlines criteria for enrolling pediatric populations in high-risk Phase 1 oncology and rare disease trials when supported by strong biological rationale and an absence of standard-of-care options.

youtube.markdown:
- Biology & Health
    - [New Research shows Anti-Aging Effects of two Molecules!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TtLj2lGpwKQ) -- Physionic
        - Clinical research evaluates the anti-aging effects of senolytic therapies, specifically combinations of dasatinib plus quercetin as well as fisetin regimens in humans.
        - Human trials examine senolytics across multiple tissues and conditions, including diabetic kidney disease, postmenopausal bone metabolism, idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, systemic sclerosis, and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis.
        - Studies assess fisetin dosing strategies for reducing senescence-related gene expression in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), alongside markers such as C12FDG associated with osteoarthritic phenotypes.
    - [414 ‒ Resistance training as we age: exercise selection, training intensity, and much more](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8IuHv7nYkDs) -- Peter Attia MD
        - Physical therapist Jeff Cavaliere outlines strategies for evolving strength training in midlife (40s, 50s, and beyond) to sustain hypertrophy and strength without compromising joint longevity.
        - The discussion covers managing fatigue and injury risk by balancing reps in reserve against training to failure, eliminating "junk volume," and implementing effective warm-up protocols.
        - Cavaliere provides a detailed muscle-by-muscle breakdown of exercise selection and modifications for the deltoids, arm musculature, chest, back, core, and lower body.
- Pure Science
    - [These ponds help support half the people on Earth](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/xlNKNnXdtN4) -- Veritasium
        - Highlights the existence of bright, electric blue ponds located within the Utah desert.
        - Raises the question of how these specific desert ponds play a critical role in supporting half of the Earth's population.
        - Notes the phenomenon of these bodies of water continuously changing color over time.
- Tech & Engineering
    - [Cette IA vous coupe la parole (et c'est fait exprès)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nj02jmGlZwc) -- Underscore_
        - Voice AI specialist Neil Zeghidour discusses technical developments and design choices in voice-based artificial intelligence.
        - Explores why certain voice AI systems are intentionally engineered to interrupt human speakers during conversation.
        - Produced in collaboration with Mammouth AI and hosted alongside Michaël de Marliave and Matthieu Lambda.
